p.src: The Planet Venus and the Handsome Monkey King came out together from the depths of the blessed cave and rose into the air on their clouds. Now Wukong's somersault cloud was unlike any other and exceedingly swift; leaving Venus far behind, he arrived first outside the Southern Gate of Heaven. Just as he was about to rein in his cloud and advance, Virūḍhaka, the Heavenly King of Growth, barred the gate with Pang, Liu, Gou, Bi, Deng, Xin, Zhang, Tao, and a whole company of mighty celestial guards armed with spears, sabers, swords, and halberds, refusing him entry. The Monkey King said, “That old fellow Venus is a treacherous rogue! If he invited me here, why has he set men brandishing blades and spears to block my way?” While he was making this uproar, Venus suddenly arrived. Wukong confronted him angrily: “You old fellow, why have you deceived me? You said you had come by the Jade Emperor's decree to summon me into his service, so why have you told these men to bar the Gate of Heaven and refuse me entry?” Venus smiled and said, “Your Majesty, calm your anger. You have never before come to this celestial court, your name is not on its registers, and these heavenly guards have never met you. How could they allow you to enter at will? Once you have met the Celestial Venerable, been entered on the immortal rolls, and had an official title registered, you may come and go as you please. Who would bar you then?” Wukong said, “If that is how it is, never mind. I shall not go in.” Venus caught him by the hand and said, “Come inside with me all the same.”

p.src: The Planet Venus led the Handsome Monkey King to the Hall of Miraculous Mist. Without waiting to be announced, he went straight before the throne and bowed in homage. Wukong stood erect beside him and offered no obeisance, merely cocking an ear to hear Venus's report. Venus memorialized, “Your servant received the sacred decree and has summoned the demon immortal here.” From behind the hanging screen, the Jade Emperor asked, “Which one is the demon immortal?” Only then did Wukong bend slightly and answer, “That would be old Sun.” The immortal ministers all turned pale with shock and cried, “How dare this wild monkey fail to prostrate himself in audience, and presume to answer, ‘That would be old Sun’! He deserves death! He deserves death!” The Jade Emperor issued a decree: “That Sun Wukong is a demon immortal from the lower realm. He has only recently attained human form and knows nothing of courtly rites, so pardon him for the present.” All the immortal ministers cried, “We thank Your Majesty for your grace.” Only then did the Monkey King make a deep ceremonial bow toward the throne. The Jade Emperor ordered the civil and military selection ministers to see where there might be a vacant post to which Sun Wukong could be appointed. From the side stepped the Lord of the Star of Military Song, who reported, “Every palace, hall, quarter, and department in Heaven has its full complement of officials. Only the Imperial Stables lack a chief superintendent.” The Jade Emperor decreed, “Then appoint him Keeper of the Heavenly Stables.” The ministers voiced their thanks for the imperial favor, while he merely gave another deep ceremonial bow toward the throne. The Jade Emperor then ordered the Wood-Virtue Star Officer to escort him to the Imperial Stables to assume his post.

p.src: The Monkey King examined the registers and verified the number of horses. The registrar of the stables was responsible for requisitioning and preparing fodder; the grooms were responsible for brushing and washing the horses, bundling hay, drawing water, and cooking feed; and the assistant and deputy superintendents helped oversee and expedite the work. The Keeper of the Heavenly Stables went without sleep day and night, tending the horses. By day he could still frolic with them, but at night he watched them diligently: whenever a horse slept, he drove it up to eat grass; whenever one wandered about, he caught it and brought it back to the manger. Whenever the heavenly horses saw him, they flattened their ears and drew their hooves together. Thus he raised them until they were plump and sleek. Before he knew it, more than half a month had passed.

p.src: One day, when there was leisure, all the stable officers prepared a banquet, both to welcome him and to congratulate him. In the midst of their merry drinking, the Monkey King suddenly set down his cup and asked, “What kind of official title is this ‘Keeper of the Heavenly Stables’ of mine?” They replied, “That itself is the name of the office.” He asked again, “What rank is this office?” They said, “It has no rank.” The Monkey King said, “No rank? Then I suppose it must be the very highest of all?” They replied, “Not high, not high. It is merely what is called ‘below the ranks.’” The Monkey King asked, “What does ‘below the ranks’ mean?” They replied, “The lowest grade. An office like this is the lowest and meanest of all; its holder is fit only to tend horses. Since Your Excellency took office, you have worked so diligently and fattened the horses, yet all you earn is a word of praise; if any grow even slightly thin or feeble, you will be reprimanded; and if any are badly injured, you will be fined and called to account.” Hearing this, the Monkey King felt a blaze of anger rise in his heart. Grinding his teeth, he cried furiously, “How dare they hold old Sun in such contempt! Old Sun was king and patriarch on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. How could they trick me into coming here to tend their horses? Tending horses is a menial task for young underlings. Is that any way to treat me? I will not do it! I will not! I am leaving!” With a crash he overturned the official desk, drew the treasure from his ear, and gave it a flourish until it grew as thick as a rice bowl. Brandishing it with all his skill, he fought his way straight out of the Imperial Stables and made directly for the Southern Gate of Heaven. The celestial guards knew that he had been entered on the immortal rolls and was the Keeper of the Heavenly Stables. Not daring to stop him, they let him fight his way out through the Gate of Heaven.

p.src: In a short while he lowered his cloud and returned to the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. There he saw the four stalwart commanders and the demon kings of the various caves drilling their troops. The Monkey King called out in a stern voice, “Little ones, old Sun is back!” The whole troop of monkeys came and kowtowed, welcomed him into the depths of the blessed cave, invited him to ascend his precious throne, and meanwhile prepared wine to celebrate his return. They all said, “Congratulations, Your Majesty! You have been in the upper realm for more than ten years; surely you have returned crowned with success and glory?” The Monkey King said, “I was there only a little over half a month. How could it have been more than ten years?” The monkeys replied, “Your Majesty, in Heaven you did not notice the passage of time. One day in Heaven is a year in the lower realm. May we ask what office Your Majesty held?” The Monkey King waved his hand and said, “Do not ask! Do not ask! It is enough to make one die of shame. That Jade Emperor has no idea how to employ talent. Seeing old Sun as I am, he appointed me to some post called ‘Keeper of the Heavenly Stables.’ It turned out to mean tending his horses, an office below even the lowest rank. When I first took office, I knew nothing of this and merely amused myself in the Imperial Stables. Only today, when I asked my colleagues, did I learn how low and mean the post was. Old Sun was greatly enraged, overturned the banquet table, refused the title, and so came back down here.” The monkeys said, “Well returned! Well returned! Here in this blessed land and sacred cave, Your Majesty reigns as king, honored and happy beyond measure. Why should you consent to serve him as a groom? Little ones, quickly bring wine to dispel His Majesty's vexation.”

p.src: While they were drinking and making merry, someone came to report, “Your Majesty, two One-Horned Demon Kings are outside and wish to see you.” The Monkey King said, “Let them in.” The Demon Kings straightened their garments, hurried into the cave, and prostrated themselves. The Handsome Monkey King asked them, “What business brings you to me?” The Demon Kings replied, “We have long heard that Your Majesty welcomes men of worth, but until now we had no means of gaining an audience. Now that Your Majesty has received a celestial appointment and returned home in triumph, we have come especially to present you with a reddish-yellow robe in celebration. If you will not disdain our lowly station but take us into your service, we too shall gladly labor for you like dogs and horses.” The Monkey King was delighted and put on the reddish-yellow robe. All those present joyfully formed ranks and bowed before him. He then appointed the Demon Kings commanders and vanguard of his forward division. After thanking him for the favor, the Demon Kings asked, “Your Majesty was in Heaven for so long. What office were you granted?” The Monkey King said, “The Jade Emperor has no regard for worthy men. He made me some sort of ‘Keeper of the Heavenly Stables.’” Hearing this, the Demon Kings said, “With such divine powers as yours, why should Your Majesty tend horses for him? Why should you not become the Great Sage Equal to Heaven?” The Monkey King was overjoyed at this suggestion and cried several times, “Excellent! Excellent! Excellent!” He ordered the four stalwart commanders, “Quickly make me a banner bearing the four great characters ‘Great Sage Equal to Heaven,’ then raise it on a pole and unfurl it. From this day forward, you are to call me only the Great Sage Equal to Heaven; you must no longer call me king. Send word to the demon kings of every cave as well, so that all may know.” But of this there is no more to tell.

p.src: Now the next day the Jade Emperor held court. Heavenly Master Zhang led the superintendent and deputy superintendent of the Imperial Stables to bow below the vermilion steps and report, “Your Majesty, the newly appointed Keeper of the Heavenly Stables, Sun Wukong, considered his office too lowly and rebelled, leaving the Heavenly Palace yesterday.” While they were speaking, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka appeared outside the Southern Gate of Heaven with a company of celestial soldiers and also reported, “For reasons unknown, the Keeper of the Heavenly Stables has fled through the gate of Heaven.” On hearing this, the Jade Emperor at once issued a decree: “Let the divine officers of both parties return to their respective posts. We shall dispatch the heavenly host to capture this monster.” From among the assembled ranks stepped the Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King Li and the Third Prince Nezha. Crossing beyond their places, they memorialized, “Your Majesty, though your humble servants possess little ability, we beg your decree that we may subdue this monster.” The Jade Emperor was greatly pleased. He appointed Li Jing, the Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King, Grand Marshal for the Subjugation of Demons, and the Third Prince Nezha Great Deity of the Three Altars and Oceanic Assembly, ordering them to muster their forces and descend to the mortal world at once.

p.src: Heavenly King Li and Nezha kowtowed in thanks and took their leave. Going straight to their palace, they mustered the three armies and their commanders, appointing the Mighty-Spirit God as vanguard, General Fish-Belly to guard the rear, and the Yaksha generals to urge on the troops. In a moment they passed through the Southern Gate of Heaven and came directly to the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. Choosing a level, sunny place, they pitched camp and sent orders for the Mighty-Spirit God to issue a challenge. Receiving the order, the Mighty-Spirit God fastened his armor neatly, brandished his ornate battle-axe, and went to the entrance of the Water-Curtain Cave. Outside the little cave entrance he saw a host of demons—wolves, insects, tigers, leopards, and their like—crowding all about, flourishing spears and swords as they leaped, fought, and roared. The Mighty-Spirit God shouted, “You accursed beasts! Hurry and tell the Keeper of the Heavenly Stables that I am a great general of Heaven, come by decree of the Jade Emperor to subdue him. Tell him to come out and surrender at once, lest all of you be maimed or slain.” The demons rushed about in panic and carried the news into the cave, crying, “Disaster! Disaster!” The Monkey King asked, “What disaster?” The demons replied, “A heavenly general stands outside. He called Your Great Sage by your official title and said that, by sacred decree of the Jade Emperor, he has come to subdue you. He demands that you go out and surrender at once, lest our lives be lost.” Hearing this, the Monkey King ordered, “Bring me my armor.” He donned his purple-gold crown, buckled on his golden armor, stepped into his cloud-treading shoes, took the compliant golden-hooped staff in hand, and led his host outside to array themselves for battle. The Mighty-Spirit God opened his eyes wide and looked. What a splendid Monkey King he saw:

p.src: The Mighty-Spirit God cried in a fierce voice, “You insolent monkey! Do you know who I am?” Hearing him, the Great Sage promptly asked, “What obscure little god are you? Old Sun has never met you. State your name at once.” The Mighty-Spirit God said, “You deceitful macaque! No wonder you do not recognize me. I am the vanguard under the Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King Li in the exalted Divine Empyrean, the Heavenly General Mighty-Spirit. By sacred decree of the Jade Emperor, I have come to accept your surrender. Quickly cast off your armor and submit to Heaven’s grace, so that all the creatures of this mountain may escape execution. If you utter so much as half a word of refusal, I shall grind you to dust in an instant.” At this the Monkey King flew into a rage and said, “You wretched little god! Do not boast so wildly or wag your tongue at such length. I would have killed you with a single blow, but then there would be no one left to carry my message. So I shall spare your life. Hurry back to Heaven and tell the Jade Emperor that he has no notion how to employ worthy men. Old Sun possesses boundless powers; why did he make me tend horses for him? Look at the title on my banner. If he promotes me according to that title, I shall not resort to arms, and Heaven and Earth will naturally remain at peace. But if he refuses, I shall immediately fight my way up to the Hall of Miraculous Mist and see whether he can remain seated on his dragon throne.” Hearing this, the Mighty-Spirit God opened his eyes wide and peered into the wind. Sure enough, outside the cave stood a tall pole bearing a banner on which were written the four great characters ‘Great Sage Equal to Heaven.’ The Mighty-Spirit God laughed coldly three times and said, “You insolent monkey! So ignorant of your proper place, yet brazen enough to behave so outrageously—you actually want to be the Great Sage Equal to Heaven! Now take a good stroke from my axe!” With that, he brought the axe down straight at the Monkey King’s head. But the Monkey King was a seasoned fighter and did not lose his composure; he raised the golden-hooped staff and met the blow. What a fine battle it was:

Hurry and carry my message! Hurry and carry my message!”

p.src: The Mighty-Spirit God returned to the camp gate and went straight before the Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King. Dropping hastily to his knees, he said, “The Keeper of the Heavenly Stables truly possesses immense divine powers. This subordinate general could not defeat him and has returned in disgrace to beg punishment.” Heavenly King Li flew into a rage and said, “This wretch has blunted the edge of our army’s spirit. Take him out and behead him!” Prince Nezha stepped out from the side, bowed, and pleaded, “Father, calm your anger and pardon the Mighty-Spirit God for now. Let your son go forth to fight him once, and we shall soon discover the measure of his strength.” The Heavenly King accepted his counsel and ordered the Mighty-Spirit God back to camp to await punishment and attend to his duties.

p.src: Wukong came forward to meet him and asked, “Whose young lad are you? What business brings you barging up to my gate?” Nezha shouted, “You insolent demon monkey! Do you not recognize me? I am Nezha, third son of the Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King. By the Jade Emperor’s command, I have come to capture you.” Wukong laughed. “Little prince, your milk teeth have not yet fallen out and your baby hair is not yet dry. How dare you boast so grandly? For now I shall spare your life and not strike you. Just look at the title written on my banner and report it respectfully to the Jade Emperor: if he grants me that rank, there will be no need to mobilize any more troops, and I shall submit of my own accord; but if my wish is denied, I shall surely fight my way up to the Hall of Miraculous Mist.” Nezha looked up and saw the four characters “Great Sage Equal to Heaven.” Nezha said, “How great can this demon monkey’s powers be, that he dares assume such a title? Stand your ground and take a stroke of my sword!” Wukong said, “I shall stand right here without moving and let you hack at me as many times as you please.” Enraged, Nezha gave a mighty shout: “Transform!” At once he changed into a being with three heads and six arms. Fierce and menacing, he wielded six weapons—the Demon-Slaying Sword, Demon-Hewing Sabre, Demon-Binding Rope, Demon-Subduing Cudgel, Embroidered Ball, and Fire Wheel—and came lunging at Wukong in a bristling assault. Seeing this, Wukong was startled and thought, “This youngster does know a few tricks after all. Do not presume too far—behold my powers!” Our splendid Great Sage cried, “Transform!” and likewise changed into a being with three heads and six arms. He shook the Gold-Banded Cudgel, and it too became three cudgels. With his six hands he grasped the three cudgels and parried the attack. The battle truly shook earth and mountains—a deadly fight indeed:

p.src: Wukong, however, was quick of hand and keen of eye. Amid the confusion, he plucked out one of his hairs and cried, “Transform!” It changed into his exact likeness, brandishing a cudgel and engaging Nezha; while his true body sprang behind Nezha and brought the cudgel down upon his left shoulder. Nezha was in the midst of working his magic when he heard the cudgel whistling through the air. He tried to dodge, but had no time to defend himself; struck by the blow, he fled in pain. He withdrew his magic, restored the six weapons to his person, and returned in defeat.

p.src: The Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King Li had already seen what happened from the battle line and was about to lead his troops forward to help when the prince suddenly appeared before him and reported, trembling, “Royal Father, that Protector of the Horses truly is formidable. Even with all my powers I could not defeat him, and he has wounded my shoulder.” The Heavenly King turned pale with alarm. “If that brute possesses such powers, how can we prevail?” The prince said, “Outside his cave gate stands a banner bearing the four characters ‘Great Sage Equal to Heaven.’ He boasted with his own mouth that if the Jade Emperor appoints him Great Sage Equal to Heaven, the whole affair will be at an end; but if he is not given that title, he will surely fight his way up to the Hall of Miraculous Mist.” The Heavenly King said, “Since that is so, let us not continue opposing him for now. We shall return to the upper realm and report his words. It will not be too late to send more celestial troops to surround and capture the brute afterward.” The prince was in pain and unable to fight again, so he returned to Heaven with the Heavenly King to make their report. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: Now see how the Monkey King returned victorious to his mountain. The demon kings of the seventy-two caves and his six sworn brothers all came to congratulate him, and they drank and made merry beyond compare in that blessed cave realm. He said to his six brothers, “Since I call myself Great Sage Equal to Heaven, you too may take the title of Great Sage.” At once the Bull Demon King among them cried aloud, “Worthy brother, you speak truly. I shall call myself the Great Sage Who Pacifies Heaven.” The Flood Dragon Demon King said, “I shall call myself the Great Sage Who Overturns the Sea.” The Peng Demon King said, “I shall call myself the Great Sage Who Confounds Heaven.” The Lion-Camel King said, “I shall call myself the Great Sage Who Moves Mountains.” The Macaque King said, “I shall call myself the Great Sage Who Penetrates the Winds.” The Snub-Nosed Monkey King said, “I shall call myself the Great Sage Who Drives the Spirits.” Thus the Seven Great Sages acted on their own authority and bestowed titles upon themselves. After making merry for the day, they all dispersed.

p.src: We now tell how the Heavenly King Li and the Third Prince led their generals straight to the Hall of Miraculous Mist and reported, “Your servants obeyed the sacred decree, marched to the lower realm, and sought to subdue the demon immortal Sun Wukong. Unexpectedly, his powers were so great that we could not prevail. We beg Your Majesty to send additional forces to destroy him.” The Jade Emperor said, “How much ability can a mere demon monkey possess, that you should need reinforcements?” The prince stepped forward again and reported, “I beg Your Majesty to pardon this servant’s capital offense. That demon monkey wields an iron cudgel. He first defeated the Mighty-Spirit God and then wounded your servant’s arm. Outside his cave gate stands a banner inscribed with the four characters ‘Great Sage Equal to Heaven.’ He says that if he is appointed to that office, he will cease hostilities at once and submit; but if he is not given that office, he will fight his way up to the Hall of Miraculous Mist.” Astonished by these words, the Jade Emperor said, “How dare this demon monkey be so outrageous? Let all the generals execute him at once.”

p.src: While they were speaking, the Great White Planet Venus again stepped out from among the ranks and reported, “That demon monkey knows only how to utter words, but not how to judge his own place. If troops are sent to fight him, I fear he cannot be subdued quickly, and the army will merely be wearied again. It would be better for Your Majesty to display boundless mercy, issue another decree of amnesty and recruitment, and let him be Great Sage Equal to Heaven. Merely grant him an empty title—an office without salary—and leave it at that.” The Jade Emperor asked, “What do you mean by ‘an office without salary’?” Venus replied, “He shall bear the title Great Sage Equal to Heaven, but be given no duties to administer and no salary. We shall simply keep him between Heaven and Earth, restrain his wayward heart, and prevent him from behaving outrageously. Thus, it is to be hoped, Heaven and Earth will remain at peace and the whole realm enjoy tranquillity.” On hearing this, the Jade Emperor said, “Let it be as you propose.” He immediately ordered an imperial decree to be issued and once more commanded Venus to take it down.

p.src: Venus went out through the Southern Gate of Heaven once more and proceeded straight to the entrance of the Water-Curtain Cave on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit to survey the scene. This time things were different from before: the display was awe-inspiring, the air thick with murderous menace, and demons of every conceivable kind were present. Every one of them brandished a sword or spear, a sabre or staff, roaring and leaping about. The moment they saw Venus, they all advanced to attack him. Venus said, “Let your chiefs come forward. I must trouble you to report to your Great Sage that I am a heavenly envoy sent by the Lord on High, and I bear a sacred decree summoning him.” The demons immediately ran inside and reported, “There is an old man outside who says he is an envoy from the upper realm and bears a decree summoning you.” Wukong said, “Excellent, excellent! I expect it is the Great White Planet Venus who came before. Though the office he summoned me to Heaven for last time proved contemptible, I did at least make one journey there and learn the roads inside and outside the heavenly gates. Since he has come again, he must surely bear good intentions.” He ordered the chiefs to unfurl all the banners, sound the drums, and marshal the ranks to welcome him. The Great Sage then led the host of monkeys forth. Wearing his crown and armor, with an ochre-yellow robe over his mail and cloud-treading shoes upon his feet, he hurried out of the cave gate, bowed in greeting, and called aloud, “Honored Star, please come inside. Forgive me for failing to welcome you sooner.”

p.src: The Gold Star stepped briskly forward, went straight into the cave, and stood facing south. He said, “I have come to inform the Great Sage that, because you previously despised the low rank of your office and absconded from the Imperial Stables, all the officials of that bureau, high and low, reported the matter to the Jade Emperor. The Jade Emperor issued a decree: ‘All who receive official appointments rise from humble rank to high. Why should he disdain a low office?’ Thereupon Heavenly King Li was sent down to the mortal world with Nezha to give battle. They did not know the extent of the Great Sage’s divine powers and were therefore defeated. On returning to Heaven, they reported: ‘The Great Sage has raised a banner and demands to be made Great Sage Equal to Heaven. The military commanders still wished to dispute the matter, but this old man risked punishment by speaking forcefully on the Great Sage’s behalf. I petitioned that the troops not be mobilized and that Your Majesty be granted an official title. The Jade Emperor approved my petition, and so I have come to invite you.’” Wukong laughed and said, “I troubled you on the previous occasion, and now I am indebted to your kindness once again. Many thanks, many thanks! But I wonder whether Heaven will truly grant me the title of Great Sage Equal to Heaven?” The Gold Star replied, “Only after I had petitioned for this very title and obtained approval did I dare accept the decree and come here. If your wish is not fulfilled, you may hold this old man alone to blame.”

p.src: Wukong was overjoyed and earnestly tried to keep the Gold Star for a banquet, but he declined. Wukong therefore mounted an auspicious cloud with him, and they arrived outside the Southern Gate of Heaven. The heavenly guards and generals all greeted him with hands respectfully clasped. They proceeded directly to the Hall of Divine Mists. The Gold Star bowed and memorialized, “Your servant was ordered to summon Sun Wukong, the Protector of the Horses. He has now arrived.” The Jade Emperor said, “Sun Wukong, come forward. I now proclaim you Great Sage Equal to Heaven. Your official rank can rise no higher, but you must on no account behave recklessly.” The monkey merely made a perfunctory salute toward the throne and said, “I thank Your Majesty for this favor.” The Jade Emperor immediately ordered the two divisions of works officials, Zhang and Lu, to erect a Residence of the Great Sage Equal to Heaven to the right of the Peach Garden. Within the residence, two bureaus were established: one called the Bureau of Peace and Quiet, and the other the Bureau of Tranquil Spirits. Each bureau was staffed with immortal clerks to attend and assist him. He also dispatched the Lords of the Five Dippers to escort Wukong to his post, and further bestowed upon him two bottles of imperial wine and ten golden flowers, instructing him to settle his heart, compose his will, and never again behave recklessly.
